paper.title: JMarkov: An Integrated Framework for Markov Chain Modeling
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 43(3), Article 29 (2017), TOMS 972
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (ACM paywall assumed, not checked). The claim rests on the shipped JUnit test KanbanTest.java in the 972.zip archive.

code.note: Java sources (jMarkov/src), JUnit tests (jMarkov/test/jmarkov), jMarkov/lib/jMarkov.jar, build.xml not in the archive root (check the Java/INSTALL.txt). Extract with unzip into a fresh directory; never run the archive's contents outside it.

field: applied probability (Markov chain and queueing model analysis)

claim.location: Java/jMarkov/test/jmarkov/KanbanTest.java, method testGetMOPsAvg: expMops[0] = 0.7003166576899312 is the average MOPS (first measure) of the Kanban model returned by kaby.getMOPsAvg(), with the default parameters of the Kanban class.
claim.metric: First entry of the average measures-of-performance vector of the Kanban model (a steady-state Markov chain solve), as returned by getMOPsAvg().
claim.paper_value: Not used: the article was not read. The value is the one written in the shipped test.

tolerance.basis: Fixed here from the shipped assertion assertArrayEquals(..., 1e-4). A steady-state linear solve reproduces doubles to far better than 1e-4, so 1e-4 is loose enough for a different JVM or solver order and tight enough to catch a changed model. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: compile the jMarkov sources and run one Kanban model solve.
cost.data_size: No external data; the Kanban model is built in code.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic Markov chain steady-state solve whose shipped expected value is a computed number (no closed form for this Kanban model is stated), with a stated absolute tolerance.
